checks.primaryClaim: 40-50 days from submission to grant, with a provisional licence at about the 15-day stage (FGD-only record; basis stated as 'Participant-reported practical duration'). FGD quote: 'It takes forty to fifty days.'
checks.sourceSays: The notified time limits are far shorter than the 40-50 days reported. The Government of Maharashtra Right to Public Services GR of 09/07/2025 (Appendix-2, the 7 services notified for the Directorate of Industrial Safety and Health) prescribes: item 1 — 'कारखाने अधिनियम,१९४८ व महाराष्ट्र कारखाने नियम,१९६३ अंतर्गत नोंदणी व परवाना देणे (अतिधोकादायक / धोकादायक कारखाने)' — 'लोकसेवा पुरविण्यासाठी विहित केलेली कालमर्यादा: ३० दिवस' [registration and grant of licence, highly hazardous / hazardous factories — 30 days]; item 2 — the same service '(अतिधोकादायक / धोकादायक कारखाने वगळून इतर कारखाने)' — '७ दिवस' [other than hazardous factories — 7 days]. Clause 4 of the GR adds 'सदर नियत कालमर्यादा ही शासकीय सुट्टीचे दिवस वगळून विहित करण्यात येत आहे' [the prescribed time limits exclude public holidays]. DISH's own procedure page states the same 7-day figure for the ordinary case: 'The application of the grant of license will be scrutinized by the department and if found ok, the conditional license will be granted within seven days.' and, for hazardous factories, 'The application of the grant of license will be scrutinized by the department and if found ok, the conditional license will be granted within sixty days. (For Hazardous Factory)'

checks.primaryClaim: VAGUE / not quantified. The FGD record gives no figure or basis: 'Participants said the fee structure should be revised (no current figure given).' The gaps array flags: 'No specific fee amount or structure was given beyond should be revised.'
checks.sourceSays: The fee is a published matrix keyed to installed horse-power against the maximum number of workers employed on any day during the year, revised with effect from the notification of 3 October 2025. Fee Schedule A is headed 'SCHEDULE - A ( Notification No. - FAC 2025/CR No. 117 (Part-2)/Labour-4 Dt. 03/10/2025.) All Factories (Except Power Generating Stations) Maximum Number of Persons to be employed on the day during the year.' It runs from Rs. 385 (NIL H.P., up to 19 workers) to Rs. 2,31,000 (above 2000 H.P., above 4000 workers); e.g. a factory with H.P. 'ABOVE 10 BUT NOT ABOVE 50' employing '51 TO 150' workers pays Rs. 11,550. Schedule B covers Power Generating Stations by installed MW capacity, from Rs. 4,620 (Upto 20 MW, upto 100 workers) to Rs. 69,300 (Over 1000 MW, over 1000 workers). The identical two schedules appear as the substituted statutory Schedules in the Maharashtra Factories (Second Amendment) Rules, 2025, published in the Maharashtra Government Gazette (Extraordinary) of 3 October 2025: 'In rule 5 of the principal Rules ... for the existing "SCHEDULE A" and "SCHEDULE B" the following SCHEDULES shall be substituted'. Rule 5(2) of the Maharashtra Factories Rules, 1963 states the basis of calculation: 'Provided further that, if the period for which the licence is applied for is one year or more but does not exceed [ten years] the fees payable therefor per year, shall be at the rates specified in this sub-rule.' Late renewal carries a graded additional fee (Schedule to rule 8): 'Upto one month 5%, Upto two months 10%, Upto three months 15%, Upto four months 20%, Upto five months and above 25%' of the fees payable for renewal.

citation.title: SCHEDULE - A (Notification No. - FAC 2025/CR No. 117 (Part-2)/Labour-4 Dt. 03/10/2025) — Factory licence fees, All Factories (Except Power Generating Stations), Directorate of Industrial Safety and Health, Maharashtra

checks.primaryClaim: MISSING / unclear. The FGD record states: 'Not discussed in the transcript; a provisional licence is issued around 15 days pending full approval, but this was not described as a deemed-approval mechanism.' The gaps array flags: 'Whether a deemed-approval mechanism exists was not discussed.'
checks.sourceSays: Deemed approval does exist, and is statutory. Rule 9 of the Maharashtra Factories Rules, 1963 ('When licence deemed to be granted or renewed') provides: 'Where an application for grant or renewal of licence is duly made in accordance with these rules and if no licence has been issued or renewed within a period of four months, the factory in respect of which the licence is to be granted or renewed shall be deemed to be duly licenced.' A later proviso shortens this sharply for the ordinary case: 'Provided further that, in case of the factory other than hazardous factory, where an application for grant or renewal of license is duly made in accordance with these rules and if no license has been issued or renewed within a period of seven working days, the factory in respect of which the license is to be granted or renewed shall be deemed to be duly licensed.' Two limits are attached. First: 'Provided that in respect of application for grant or renewal of licence which has already been refused, if it is made again, the factory in respect of which it is made, shall not be deemed to be licensed until the licence is actually granted or renewed.' Second, the Explanation: 'For the purpose of this rule, an application for the grant or renewal of a licence shall be deemed to have been duly made only if it is in the prescribed form and is filled in with all relevant particulars and further is accompanied by a treasury receipt [or Demand Draft or Electronic Payment] or an invoice for book adjustment, as the case may be, for payment of the fees in accordance with the Schedule annexed to rule 5.'

checks.primaryClaim: Only three items, expressly not itemised: 'Consent to Operate (from the Pollution Control Board)', 'Safety audit report (empanelled third-party auditor)', 'Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) report (empanelled third-party auditor)', with the note 'The full annual document set re-uploaded each year was not itemised beyond these'.
checks.sourceSays: DISH publishes the full checklist — 22 numbered items under 'Necessary Documents for Factory Registration and Grant of Licence for Other Than Hazardous Factory and Hazardous Factory': '1. Recent Passport size Photograph & Signature to be uploaded'; '2. Any one of the following documents to be uploaded as a identity proof — Pan card / Aadhar Card / Driving licence / Passport / Voting card'; '3. A) If Public Ltd./Private Ltd. company — List of director along with residential address; Memorandum of Association; Form no. 32/12 of the Companies Act...; Board of Directors resolution about appointment of Director as occupier (Certified by Company Secretary); B) In case of Partnership Firm — Partnership Deed...; NOC of other partner...'; '4. If women workers are working in the factory then information about sexual harassment Complaint Committee'; '5. List of Raw material, intermediate, byproducts and finish product along with its quantity'; '6. Any one of the following document: Ownership document- leave and licence agreement / MIDC allotment letter / Form no. 7/12 / Tax receipt'; '7. Any one of the following document: Local authority NOC / NOC from Grampachayat / NOC from MunicipalCorporation/Municipal Council/Corporation / NOC from MIDC / MPCB consent letter'; '8. Any one of the following document: Electricity Bill / Load Sanction letter'; '9. Declaration'; '10. Acceptance letter of Director as appointment of Occupier'; '11. Process flow chart'; '12. Description of Manufacturing Process'; '13. Rough Sketch of factory building showing Emergency Exits'; items 14-21 are marked '(Required for Hazardous Factory)' and cover raw-material storage lists, finished/intermediate products and toxic emissions, hazards and controls, 'Material Safety Data Sheets in respect of hazardous chemicals', 'Process & Instrumentation Diagram', chemical reactions, the health-and-safety policy and 'Duly signed copy of Form no.1'; '22. Any other documents, if required, may be uploaded'. The renewal checklist is separate and shorter (10 items), headed by '1. Old Licence', '2. Duly signed copy of Form no.1', '3. Electricity Bill as a proof for installed H.P.' and '9. A Copy of Letter of Approval of Plan by DISH'.

checks.primaryClaim: Six steps; filed online via the LMS portal through MAITRI/MAITRI 2.0, automation level 'partial'; department raises queries about 15 days after submission; provisional licence at about day 15; 'Inspecting officer visits and conveys compliance requirements orally'; full licence after queries and inspection. Remark: 'the process is described as end-to-end online, but interaction with the officer continues to be required.'
checks.sourceSays: The official procedure matches the online filing route and the inspection requirement. DISH's procedure page lists: '1. Log on to the web site www.lms.mahaonline.gov.in'; '2. Click on "Create Employer User Profile"'; '3. Fill the information and complete the Registration procedure on MAITRI portal.'; '4. Fill the CAF (Common Application Form)'; '5. Select the service provided as Registration and Grant of Licence from Directorate of Industrial Safety and Health Department.'; '6. Fill the information and complete Form no.1 and upload the duly signed copy of the same on the portal'; '7. Upload recent photograph and signature Occupier.'; '8. Upload necessary documents'; '9. Pay the necessary fees online & submit online application'; '12. The issue certificate can be downloaded from the same login id'; '13. The application will be rejected if any incomplete or wrong information is furnished.'; '14. The applicant can apply again within 30 days from the rejection.' That inspection precedes grant is stated in DISH's Citizen Charter: 'सर्व फॉर्मची पूर्तता व नकाशाप्रमाणे इमारत व मशिनरीची मांडणी असल्याची तपासणी केल्यानंतर कारखान्यास परवाना दिला जातो.' [the licence is given to the factory after verification/inspection that all forms are complete and that the building and machinery are laid out as per the approved plan], and the same Charter confirms periodic inspection: 'कारखान्याचे निरीक्षण याद्दच्छिक पध्दतीने करण्यात येते. सर्व अतिधोकादायक, धोकादायक व रासायनिक कारखान्यांचे निरीक्षण वर्षातून एकदा करण्यात येते.' [factory inspection is carried out on a random basis; all highly hazardous, hazardous and chemical factories are inspected once a year]. The Charter also confirms the pre-licensing plan-approval dependency the FGD step 1 implies: 'संबंधितांना इमारतीचे व मशिनरीच्या मांडणीचे नकाशे मंजूर करुन घ्यावे लागतात. नकाशे मंजूर करुन घेण्याची प्रक्रीया ऑनलाईन करण्यात आलेली आहे. परवान्याचे नुतनीकरण देखील ऑनलाईन करण्यात आलेले आहे.' Nothing in the official sources describes the query rounds or the oral communication of compliance requirements that the FGD reports.

remarks: BIGGEST SINGLE FINDING, outside the five check keys but material to the dashboard: the FGD record states the licence validity is one year and that the same documents are re-uploaded 'every year'. Official sources contradict this. Rule 5-A of the Maharashtra Factories Rules, 1963 provides for 'the grant of licence therefor for a period not exceeding ten year'; rule 8(1) allows 'An application for the renewal of licence for a period not exceeding [ten years]'; Form 1 (both the version hosted on DISH's Forms page and the version substituted by the October 2025 gazette) asks for 'The period for which license or renewal of license is applied for (not exceeding ten years)'; and DISH's own Citizen Charter says in terms: 'दरवर्षी नुतनीकरण करावे लागत असे परंतू ही मुदत दहा वर्षापर्यंत वाढविल्यामुळे कारखानदारांना सोयीचे झाले आहे.' [earlier renewal had to be done every year, but since this period has been extended up to ten years it has become convenient for factory owners]. The annual-renewal burden the FGD participants describe therefore appears to be a matter of practice or of applicants electing a one-year period, not a legal requirement. Rule 6(2) does fix the expiry date at '31st day of December next following', so a licence always runs to a 31 December, but for up to ten of them.

The 7-day / 30-day statutory limits and the 7-working-day deemed-licence proviso are in tension with the 40-50 days the FGD reports and with the 'provisional licence at the 15-day stage' practice participants described. The official analogue of that provisional licence is DISH's 'conditional license ... granted within seven days'. A reviewer should read the contradiction as practice-versus-notified-limit, not as the FGD being wrong about what businesses experience.

DISH's own web pages are partly out of date against the July 2025 RTS GR. The Approval of Plans page still states 'Time-Line for providing Service (Days) as per RTPS Act, 2015 :- Approval of Plans under Factories Act 1948 - 21 Days', whereas Appendix-2 of the GR dated 09/07/2025 notifies 30 days for that service. The Registration page's 'sixty days (For Hazardous Factory)' likewise exceeds the 30 days now notified for hazardous factories.

Fee-schedule provenance caveat: the Fee Schedule A and B PDFs on mahadish.in both cite 'Notification No. - FAC 2025/CR No. 117 (Part-2)/Labour-4 Dt. 03/10/2025', while the English text of the gazette carrying the identical substituted schedules (Maharashtra Factories (Second Amendment) Rules, 2025, dated 3rd October 2025) cites 'No. FAC 2025/CR No. 117 (Part-1)/Labour-4'. The figures are identical in both; only the Part-1/Part-2 suffix differs. Both documents were fetched and read this session; the discrepancy is reported as found and not resolved.

The consolidated 'Maharashtra Factories Rules, 1963 - As on 01/09/2025' PDF predates the 3 October 2025 amendment, so its printed Schedules A and B still carry the older 2012/2015 figures (e.g. Rs. 350 instead of Rs. 385 at the lowest slab). Rule 9 (deemed licence), rule 5-A, rule 6 and rule 8, quoted above, are not amended by the October 2025 notification and so are current.

Form 2 (नमुना २) is still published on DISH's Forms/Download page and still bears '(In triplicate)' and a 'Court Fee Stamp of Rs.10/-', but it is legacy: rule 8(1)'s reference to Form 2 was replaced by Form 1 in 2015, and the Maharashtra Factories (Second Amendment) Rules, 2025 make the whole process electronic — 'made electronically in Form 1', 'the words "in duplicate" shall be deleted', 'in sub-rule (1), the words "in triplicate" shall be deleted', and rule 14 substituted to read 'The notice of occupation, along with supporting documents, shall be submitted in Form 1 electronically.' The 2025 Form 1 also requires a 'Digital Signature of Occupier' and 'Digital Signature of Manager' and records 'Amount of fees Rs._______ paid online vide order No. _________'. This is independent support for the FGD's 'automationLevel: partial' being an understatement of the legal position, and for its complaint that paper/manual steps persist in practice.

No official source was found that corroborates the FGD's claim that a safety audit report and a HIRA report from an empanelled third-party auditor are required documents for grant or renewal of the factory licence. They do not appear in either the 22-item grant checklist or the 10-item renewal checklist on mahadish.in; the 2025 Form 1 asks only for 'Date of last safety audit (if applicable)'. Maharashtra does have separate Factories (Safety Audit) Rules, 2014 (amended 2024), listed on the DISH Acts & Rules page, which may be the real source of that obligation, but that document was not fetched and read this session, so nothing is asserted about it.

Similarly, the FGD's 'Consent to Operate (from the Pollution Control Board)' appears in the official checklist only as one of five alternatives at item 7 ('Local authority NOC / NOC from Grampachayat / NOC from MunicipalCorporation... / NOC from MIDC / MPCB consent letter'), i.e. the official position is that an MPCB consent letter is one acceptable way of satisfying a local-NOC requirement, not a mandatory separate attachment. That nuance is worth putting to the department.

The issuing authority the FGD record could not name is confirmed: the Directorate of Industrial Safety and Health (औद्योगिक सुरक्षा व आरोग्य संचालनालय), Maharashtra. Form 4 as substituted in October 2025 is headed 'Directorate of Industrial Safety and Health, Maharashtra State' and signed 'Chief Inspector/Deputy Chief Inspector'; Appendix-2 of the RTS GR names the designated officers as the Director, DISH Mumbai (hazardous) and the Joint Director of the concerned division (non-hazardous), with first and second appellate authorities specified for each service.

DISH's Citizen Charter states the Maharashtra applicability threshold and the advance-filing expectation: a licence is required where 20 or more workers work with the aid of power, or 40 or more without power, and 'ज्या आस्थापनांना कारखाने अधिनियमाखाली नोंदणी करुन परवाना आवश्यक असतो त्यांनी किमान १५ दिवस आधी विहीत नमुना क्र.१ भरुन त्यासोबत परिशिष्टामध्ये नमुद केल्याप्रमाणे शुल्कासह ऑनलाईन पध्दतीने अर्ज करावा' [those needing registration and a licence should apply online in the prescribed Form 1 with the fee at least 15 days in advance]. The Charter PDF is a scanned, non-Unicode document; its Marathi was read by rendering the pages to images, not by text extraction.
Transport note: every citation above was fetched over https. No http-only source was used, no certificate verification was disabled and no 403/WAF check was worked around.

Sources attempted but not usable, and therefore not cited: https://rts.maharashtra.gov.in/ (the Maharashtra State Right to Service Commission site) — curl failed with 'Recv failure: Connection reset by peer'; https://mahadish.in/rts and https://mahadish.in/citizen_charter — these paths exist but return a 2.8 KB stub, the real content being at https://mahadish.in/mandatory_disclosures, which was used instead. The transactional portal lms.mahaonline.gov.in was not retried this session (the source-list compilation pass had already recorded it as unreachable), so nothing here is asserted about portal behaviour, file-size limits or night-time downtime — the FGD's portal complaints are neither confirmed nor contradicted.
